etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Middle English fulfillen, from Old English fullfyllan (“to fill full”), corresponding to ful- +‎ fill.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To satisfy, carry out, bring to completion (an obligation, a requirement, etc.).

quote.citation: 2013 February 6, Hideo Otake, “Revising the Interpretation of the Japanese Economy”, in Michio Muramatsu, Frieder Naschold, editors, State and Administration in Japan and Germany: A Comparative Perspective on Continuity and Change‎[1], page 319:
quote.text: Japanese retail stores have strove to, and have succeeded in, fulfilling these severe demands, and in doing so, have constantly had to innovate both technologically and institutionally in order to keep up with the competition.

definitions.definition: (transitive) To emotionally or artistically satisfy; to develop one's gifts to the fullest.
(transitive) To obey, follow, comply with (a rule, requirement etc.).
(business) To package, distribute, or ship goods.
(archaic) To fill full; fill to the utmost capacity; fill up.

quote.citation: 1870, James Thomson, The City of Dreadful Night:
quote.text: The silence which benumbs or strains the senseFulfils with awe the soul's despair unweeping
